Investor Relations - YUASA TRADING CO., LTD.|website=www.yuasa.co.jp}} Yuasa Iron Works began producing storage batteries in 1915, and three years later Yuasa Storage Battery Co., Ltd was established.{{cite web|url=http://www.gs-yuasa.com/en/company/history.php|title=History - About - GS Yuasa|first=GS|last=Yuasa|website=www.gs-yuasa.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.yuasa.co.uk/company/history/yuasa-battery-corporation/|title=Yuasa Battery Corporation - Yuasa}} Soon after, Yuasa Storage Battery Co., Ltd began making Japan's first automotive batteries.{{cite web |url=http://www.yuasa.com.au/asp/index.asp?pgid=11295 |title=Yuasa | History |access-date=2016-02-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160228232332/http://yuasa.com.au/asp/index.asp?pgid=11295 |archive-date=2016-02-28 }} In 1925, Yuasa began making dry cells, and in 1941 they began making alkaline cells. The dry battery business was later spun off into Yuasa Dry Battery Co., Ltd, which later merged back into Yuasa Storage Battery Co., Ltd to form Yuasa Battery Co, Ltd, later renamed to Yuasa Corporation. === GS === [[File:Shimazu Genzō I.jpg|left|thumb|235x235px|Genzo Shimadzu Sr.]] [[File:Shimazu Genzō II 3.jpg|left|thumb|223x223px|Genzo Shimadzu Jr.]] In 1904, {{Nihongo|{{ill|Genzo Shimadzu Jr.|ja|島津源蔵 (2代目)}}|島津 源蔵|Shimazu Genzō|b. 1869 d. 1951}} developed a high-capacity lead-acid battery to supply backup power to his factory during outages of Kyoto's then unreliable power grid. The Japanese navy purchased 400 units of this battery. Shimadzu established Japan Storage Battery Co., Ltd in 1917{{cite web|url=http://ieeemilestones.ethw.org/Milestones:Birth_and_Growth_of_Primary_and_Secondary_Battery_Industries_in_Japan|title=Milestones:Birth and Growth of Primary and Secondary Battery Industries in Japan - IEEE Milestones Wiki|website=ieeemilestones.ethw.org|date=27 May 2015 }} and began producing automotive batteries in 1919. In 1938 they began producing alkaline batteries and in 1940 they began making high-pressure mercury lamps. '''GS''' was established in 1917[http://www.gs-yuasa.com/us/corporate/pdf/a4_history(e).pdf Japan Storage Battery History] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212044617/http://www.gs-yuasa.com/us/corporate/pdf/a4_history(e).pdf |date=2013-12-12 }}, GS Yuasa Corporation history viewed 2013-8-5 and is an abbreviation comprising the initials of Genzou Shimadzu Jr. who founded Japan Storage Battery in 1917. He was also the second president of [[Shimadzu Corporation]] founded in 1875 by his father, {{Nihongo|{{ill|Genzo Shimadzu Sr.|ja|島津源蔵 (初代)}}|島津 源蔵|Shimazu Genzō|b. 1839 d. 1894}}. === GS Yuasa === In 2004, Yuasa Corporation merged with Japan Storage Battery to form GS Yuasa Corporation. As of 2014, GS Yuasa had 9 plants for manufacturing industrial lead-acid and NiCd batteries and 5 plants for Li-Ion cells. GS Yuasa also sells other products including power supplies, lamps and motorcycle batteries.{{cite web |url=http://sajapan.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/GS-YUASA@SA-EMBASSY-ECONOMIC-OFFICE-WORKSHOP-on-25-November-2014.pdf |title=Office workshop |date=25 November 2014 |website=sajapan.org |access-date=1 February 2016 |archive-date=27 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527180139/http://sajapan.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/GS-YUASA@SA-EMBASSY-ECONOMIC-OFFICE-WORKSHOP-on-25-November-2014.pdf |url-status=dead }} Now the top power sports battery producer, Yuasa provides nearly 90% of the batteries used in power sport vehicles in [[North America]].{{cite news|url=http://yuasabatteries.com/history.php|title=About Yuasa - Yuasa Batteris Inc - Vehicle & Industrial Batteries|newspaper=Yuasa Battery, Inc|archive-date=2018-06-04|access-date=2013-03-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180604235551/http://yuasabatteries.com/history.php|url-status=dead}} == Joint ventures == GS Yuasa was one of the active players in the [[electric vehicle]] battery industry during the late 2000s to early 2010s when numerous battery vendors largely from Japan had formed alliances with car manufacturers to enter the novel market of EV. === Lithium Energy Japan === In 2007, GS Yuasa and [[Mitsubishi Motors]] have formed an alliance and started a joint venture named '''Lithium Energy Japan (LEJ)''' that develops and manufactures lithium-ion batteries for automotive and industrial use. The [[Mitsubishi i-MiEV]], the first mass-produced electric car, was equipped with the batteries from LEJ.{{Cite web|date=2010-04-14|title=JAPAN: Lithium Energy plans third lithium-ion cell plant|url=https://www.just-auto.com/news/lithium-energy-plans-third-lithium-ion-cell-plant_id104034.aspx|access-date=2020-10-08|website=www.just-auto.com|archive-date=2020-10-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009051554/https://www.just-auto.com/news/lithium-energy-plans-third-lithium-ion-cell-plant_id104034.aspx|url-status=dead}} === Blue Energy Co. === In 2009, [[Honda]] partnered with GS Yuasa to set up an EV battery supplier '''Blue Energy Co. (BEC)'''. The HVs from Honda including [[Honda Civic Hybrid|Civic Hybrid]] have been powered by lithium-ion batteries manufactured by BEC which has a production facility in [[Kyoto]].{{Cite web|title=GS Yuasa will triple Li-ion battery supply to Honda|url=https://www.greencarcongress.com/2012/02/gs-yuasa-will-triple-li-ion-battery-supply-to-honda.html|access-date=2020-10-08|website=Green Car Congress}} However, Honda has been in search for new partners aside from BEC since the late 2010s, teaming up with various companies like [[Nissan]], [[General Motors]], and [[Contemporary Amperex Technology|CATL]].{{Cite web|date=2018-06-10|title=Honda teams with GM for lithium batteries|url=https://www.eenewsautomotive.com/news/honda-teams-gm-lithium-batteries-0|access-date=2020-10-08|website=eeNews Automotive|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Honda partners with CATL on Li-ion EV batteries; 56 GWh by 2027|url=https://www.greencarcongress.com/2019/02/20190206-hondacatl.html|access-date=2020-10-08|website=Green Car Congress|archive-date=2022-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209110920/https://www.greencarcongress.com/2019/02/20190206-hondacatl.html|url-status=dead}} === Lithium Energy & Power GmbH === In 2014, [[Robert Bosch GmbH]] and GS Yuasa partnered on next-gen Li-ion EV battery with the ambitious goals to double energy density and make it to mass market by 2020 while lowering the cost by half as well. The venture has ended without a meaningful outcome after Bosch has decided to outsource battery cell manufacturing in 2018.{{Cite web|title=Bosch ist eigene Batteriezellfertigung zu teuer|url=https://www.kfz-betrieb.vogel.de/bosch-ist-eigene-batteriezellfertigung-zu-teuer-a-690808/|access-date=2020-10-08|website=www.kfz-betrieb.vogel.de|date=28 February 2018 |language=de}} == Overseas operations == === United States === ==== Yuasa Battery Inc ==== Yuasa Battery, Inc (U.S.A.) was established in 1965. In 1979, Yuasa began producing motorcycle batteries in a joint venture established with General Battery Corporation in Laureldale, PA a few years earlier. Today, Yuasa Battery Inc supplies batteries for motorcycles, scooters, personal watercraft, [[all-terrain vehicles]] (ATV), and side by sides ([[Side by Side (UTV)|UTV]]). ==== Yuasa-Exide Inc ==== In 1987 [[Fruit of the Loom]] sold its General Battery Corporation to [[Exide Technologies|Exide]] Corporation.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=1987-03-24 |title=COMPANY NEWS; Fruit of the Loom |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/03/24/business/company-news-fruit-of-the-loom.html |access-date=2026-05-27 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} In 1991, Yuasa Battery Co. Ltd (Japan) bought Exide's industrial battery division, forming Yuasa-Exide Inc,{{Cite web |title=Yuasa Battery buys Exide's industrial division |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1991/06/11/Yuasa-Battery-buys-Exides-industrial-division/6601676612800/ |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=UPI |language=en}}{{cite web|url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-06-12/business/25787682_1_exide-spokesman-industrial-batteries-exide-corp|title=Archives - Philly.com|website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]}}{{dead link|date=October 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} later renamed to Yuasa Inc. In 2000, a management buyout of Yuasa Inc's industrial battery business formed [[EnerSys|Enersys]]. Today, Enersys sells a wide variety of batteries. === Europe === In 1981, Yuasa established a company in the UK to manufacture [[VRLA battery|VRLA batteries]] and another for sales and distribution. They later established companies in Germany, France, and Italy for sales and distribution. In 1988, Yuasa Corporation acquired a 50% share in Lucas Batteries Ltd, forming Lucas-Yuasa Batteries Ltd. Yuasa purchased the remaining 50% of Lucas Batteries in 1997, creating Yuasa Automotive Batteries Europe Ltd, which marketed automotive batteries under the Lucas brand and other names until 2006, when Yuasa began marketing automotive batteries in Europe under its own name. In 2002, Yuasa Battery Europe Ltd was formed as the parent company for Yuasa's various European sales companies.{{Cite news |title=Yuasa Battery Europe company history |url=http://www.yuasa.co.uk/company/history/yuasa-battery-europe-ltd/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011200717/http://www.yuasa.co.uk/company/history/yuasa-battery-europe-ltd/ |archive-date=2025-10-11 |access-date=2026-05-27 |work=Yuasa |language=en-GB}} Today, Yuasa Battery Europe Ltd sells a variety of batteries. === Australia=== Century Batteries Australia is a division of Century Yuasa Batteries Pty Ltd and an affiliate of the GS Yuasa Corporation.{{cite web|url=http://www.centurybatteries.com.au/about-us|title=About Us - Century Batteries|website=www.centurybatteries.com.au}} === Vietnam === GS Battery VietNam Co., Ltd is a company 100% foreign owned capital, joint venture between GS-Yuasa Corporation and Mitsubishi Corporation.{{Cite web|last=G7Auto.vn|title=Ắc quy GS|url=https://g7auto.vn/gs2|access-date=2021-11-08|website=g7auto.vn|language=vi}}{{Cite web|last=GSbattery.vn|title=Ắc quy GS|url=https://gsbattery.vn/|access-date=2021-09-28|website=gsbattery.vn|language=vi}}{{Cite web|last=acquygs.com.vn|title=Ắc quy GS|url=https://acquygs.com.vn/ac-quy-gs/|access-date=2024-06-17|website=acquygs.com.vn|language=vi}}{{Cite web|last=acquyhoaphat.com|title=Ắc quy GS|url=https://acquyhoaphat.com/gioi-thieu/ac-quy-gs/2667/|access-date=2024-07-23|website=acquyhoaphat.com|language=vi}} == Miscellaneous == === Boeing 787 === {{Main|2013 Boeing 787 Dreamliner grounding}}The parent company in Japan was linked to [[Boeing 787 Dreamliner battery problems|faulty electrics used in Boeing's 787 Dreamliner plane]].[[Hiroko Tabuchi]] and Bettina Wassener.
